messages:
sasha: Heads up — product asked for per-customer cost + latency dashboards for a set of strategic accounts. Requirements: isolated views, noisy-neighbor alerts, 90d retention. Can runtime/ingest teams outline what metrics we can realistically provide?

runtime-eng: We can emit latency, token_count, queue_length, and model_variant labels at request finish. But high-cardinality labels (customer_id) will explode Prometheus-style cardinality. Need an ingest-side aggregation plan.

eng-platform: Agree. We should avoid raw customer_id on high-card metrics. Proposal: emit a hashed customer_id for traceability and have the ingest cluster map hashes -> orgs for UI rendering in a secure service. That keeps TSDB cardinality bounded while enabling per-org dashboards.

observability-bot: doc: https://redwood.internal/observability/metrics-contracts — new section 'per-tenant-aggregation' created.

lina: For noisy-neighbor detection i suggest 3 signals: 1) sudden sustained increase in 95p latency vs baseline, 2) token rate per minute spike, 3) per-worker queue depth. Combine with model and region for context.

security: Important: do NOT include prompt or response text in metrics or labels. Also retention and access controls: per-org dashboards must honor RBAC and redact org ids in logs unless requested with a security review.

runtime-eng: Implementation detail: we can emit metrics like:
```
# example metric emitted at request end
redwood_inference_latency_ms{cust_hash="h_8f3a",model="redwood-1.0",route="chat",shard="gpu-a"} 124
redwood_tokens_processed_total{cust_hash="h_8f3a",model="redwood-1.0"} 512
```
Ingest pipeline can fold cust_hash into per-tenant rollups for dashboards.

sam: From console/UX side, we need an API for "enable per-org dashboard" and rollout gating. Ideally a single toggle + retention dropdown (30/90/365). Also want canary -> gradual enable so we don't overload ingest.

kevin: On quotas: if we add per-tenant telemetry, we should also add a lightweight per-org sampling config to avoid top customers generating huge volumes. Runtime can sample 1% of requests for full detail and emit rollup metrics for all requests.

eng-platform: Two integration patterns: 1) low-cardinality metrics with cust_hash + per-tenant rollup job, 2) high-detail events sent to object store (parquet) for selected customers only (requires opt-in & storage quota). Which do we want to standardize?

lina: For noisy neighbor alerts we can run detection in stream (kafka stream) using sliding windows. Example rule: if 95p latency increases >30% vs 1h baseline AND token_rate > X, fire alert. We'll produce alert payload with org id (hashed) + severity + suggested mitigations.

security: Make sure mapping service that resolves cust_hash->org is access-controlled and audited. HSM/KMS calls not needed but logs must be scrubbed.

runtime-eng: One more practical thing — we need a simple proto for telemetry:
```proto
message InferenceTelemetry {
  string cust_hash = 1;
  string model = 2;
  string route = 3;
  int64 latency_ms = 4;
  int64 tokens = 5;
  string shard = 6;
}
```
This keeps payload small and parsable.

sam: UX: when rollout is enabled we should show an "ingest cost estimate" in the console prior to enabling. Use historical token_rate and sampling to extrapolate.

kevin: Ops ask — add a hard quota for telemetry writes per organization; alert us when a single org is > 50% of ingest cost. Also provide a way to pause telemetry for that org automatically.

eng-platform: Action items: 1) runtime to publish proto + initial metric labels (runtime-eng) 2) ingest team to design per-tenant rollup job and hashing map service (eng-platform + runtime-eng) 3) observability to add noisy-neighbor detection job (lina) 4) security to sign-off on mapping and retention (security) 5) console to add toggle + cost estimate UX + rollout API (sam) 6) ops add telemetry quotas and pause knob (kevin).

sasha: Thanks all — let's sync on Tuesday 10am PT to review the proto + rollup design. @eng-platform @runtime-eng @observability-bot please add docs to the metrics-contracts page before then. :thumbsup:
